finding.claim: isLinkLocal() returns false for fe80::/10 addresses with nonzero bits 10-63 (e.g. fe80:1::1, febf::1), because it requires bits 0-63 to exactly equal fe80:0:0:0, while getType() classifies the same addresses as 'Link-local unicast'.
finding.source: Untrusted IPv6 literal passed to Address6 and classified with isLinkLocal() (e.g. SSRF allow/deny filter).
finding.sink: Boolean returned by isLinkLocal(), documented as backing trust-boundary decisions.

trace.note: isLinkLocal() entry; embedded IPv4 branch does not apply to these addresses
Exact-equality comparison of getBitsBase2(0,64) against 1111111010 followed by 54 zeros (literal confirmed to be 64 bits)
getType() matches fe80::/10 via isHostInSubnet and returns 'Link-local unicast'
getScope() treats 'Link-local unicast' as link local, so the library disagrees with itself

finding.guards_checked: Embedded-IPv4 delegation (ipv6.ts:1247) does not apply; fromURL rejects % in hosts (ipv6.ts:213-269, constants RE_URL), so zone-scoped link-local targets are not reachable through that path; real link-local connects generally need a zone ID, limiting practical impact.

finding.claim: AddressError.parseMessage on the bad-character path inserts raw input characters (<, >, ", ', &) unescaped, contradicting the documented contract that it is HTML-escaped and safe to insert as-is.
finding.source: Any string passed to new Address6(...), e.g. from a form field in an address-inspector UI.
finding.sink: parseMessage HTML fragment, documented as safe to insert as-is.

trace.note: parse() matches bad characters on the raw (v4-rewritten) address
replace wraps each bad character in $1 without escaping $1
Doc comment claims the address content is HTML-escaped and safe to insert as-is

finding.guards_checked: Text-content injection is blocked because every bad character is followed by , so a < cannot start a tag and a & cannot form an entity. The non-bad-character path at ipv6.ts:817 only sees [0-9a-f:/%]. The v4-octet path at ipv6.ts:762-763 escapes its prefix. Exploitation requires the consumer to place parseMessage inside a quoted attribute, where a raw " breaks out.

finding.source: Caller-supplied string passed to the public v6.helpers.simpleGroup (exported via src/ip-address.ts:7).
finding.sink: HTML fragment returned to the caller.
